chunks: As for what Saʿd narrated from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from one who informed him, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning:

A man prays while a woman prays beside him. He said: There is no harm. The proper way to understand this report is that it is to be understood as referring to when the man is slightly ahead of the woman, such that his saying, ‘she prays beside him,’ is in a figurative sense due to her closeness to him.

key_terms.الْخَبَرِ: the report or hadith being interpreted
key_terms.الْمَجَازِ: figurative usage, not strict literal alignment
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the woman in relation to prayer positioning
key_terms.بِحِذَائِهِ: beside him or aligned with him
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection

ai.seo_question: Can a man and a woman perform salat (prayer) side by side?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling of a man and a woman praying in close proximity. It explains that the permissibility mentioned in the narration is understood to apply when the man is slightly ahead, so that the wording 'beside him' is interpreted loosely because of nearness.
